why: Defines ṣarm as crop cutting, the harvest action stated in 16a.
Reads the oath as a secret all-crop harvest, supporting 16a and 16d's no-exception contrast.
Historical reports on the garden's owner and location; the claims give neither detail.
Reports the father's gifts and gleaning custom, grounding the poor share withheld in 16b.
Explains the sons' resentment and plan to exclude the needy, supporting 16b.
Discusses the early account's omission of names and dates, which the claims do not address.
Rejects later tree-removal legends and leaves the garden's date unstated; neither point appears in claims.
Uses Yunus's worldly-life parable as a parallel for the garden's sudden-loss lesson in 16d.
Identifies the tested plural as deniers and oath-breakers, specifying 16a's referent.
Reports the famine as one interpretation of Quraysh's trial parallel in 16a.
Reports a rival Quraysh parallel for the planned deprivation in 16a–16b.
Rejects the Badr reading as anachronistic and says the warning targets tyrants generally, qualifying 16a.
Places the garden's consequence in worldly punishment, supporting 16d's loss lesson.
Reads the parable as sudden removal of blessing, supporting the ruin and loss points in 16c–16d.
Interprets the parable as a warning about Quraysh leaders' authority and futile repentance; claims omit those themes.
Reads tested plural as Quraysh leadership collectively, specifying 16a's denier referent.
Interprets 'the garden' as generic rather than historical; the page makes no claim about its identity.
Explains owners' confidence from prior weather survival; the claims do not state their motive.
Identifies Quraysh's warning, poor exclusion, garden ruin, and withheld produce loss in 16a–16d.
Reports the sons' dawn plan against the poor and its ruin, supporting 16a–16d.
Links Quraysh's rejection to lost prosperity, an interpretation of the deniers' test in 16a.
Reports a dawn withholding plan from poor heirs, supporting 16a–16b and 16d's retained-produce point.
Dates Al-Qalam's composition as early Makkan; the page does not discuss chronology.
Reports which Al-Qalam verse ranges early commentators classify as Madinan or Makkan.
Names miserliness as cause, with lost harvest supporting 16b's exclusion and 16c–16d's consequences.
